# 会话管理 · dsh-session-keeper
English | 中文
Turn the dsh sidebar into something you can actually manage: **category trees, drag reordering, pinn

ing, an archive section, and a delete bin you can undo from.**
Every Workspace keeps its own categor
ies, every session belongs to at most one category, and a deleted session goes to the bin instead of
session belongs to at most one category, and a deleted session goes to the bin instead of vanishing.

| Package | `dsh-session-keeper` |
| Display name | **会话管理** (Session Manager) — the tab under Setti

ngs → Plugins |
| Version | `1.2.1` |
| License | MIT |
| Shape | Host entry + Web client bundle + C
ordis profile patch in one package. No separate Client or Bundle package. |

> **Where this code comes from.** This is a maintained fork of
> ht719/dsh-session-categories (`0.1.

0`, MIT).
> The upstream package will not open on a current dsh at all. This repository ports it and

then extends it.
> Every change records **where it came from** (upstream baseline, an idea taken fr

om a competing plugin, or a
> user report) in CHANGELOG.md; the porting details live in FORK-NOTES.m

d.
>
> **Do not install this together with the upstream package.** `dsh-session-keeper` and
> `@deep

seek-ai/dsh-session-categories` both claim the `sidebar.workspaces` slot and both open the
> same st

orage domain (`session_categories`, version 0). Side by side they fight over the sidebar and
> write
into one category document. Pick one — this fork, or upstream.
## Why this fork exists
Upstream `dsh-session-categories@0.1.0` shipped 2026-08-19 against an older dsh prerelease. dsh has

since
**removed the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime` package**, and the upstream client bundle stil
d the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime` package**, and the upstream client bundle still requires it:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The dsh module loader resolves a client bundle's `require` calls against the plugin's declared `inje

ct` peers.
An unresolvable require throws while the bundle is being materialised, so the `sidebar.wo

rkspaces` slot entry
crashes on mount. The official sidebar takes the slot back, and because the cra

sh happens during shell boot
the window never finishes opening — which looks like "dsh is dead".
This branch **rebuilds the bundle from source** rather than patching `lib/`, so a plugin reinstall c

annot
undo the fix. Upstream is also missing two things: `Rows.module.css` is absent from the reposi

tory even though
`Rows.tsx` imports it, and the reconstructed stylesheet once carried a truncated `@

keyframes row-in` block —
a single broken at-rule silently invalidates every rule after it. Both are

repaired here; see
FORK-NOTES.md and BUILD.md.
## Features
### 1. Category trees

- **Per-Workspace isolation**: a category in Workspace A never leaks into Workspace B.
- **Multi-lev

el nesting**: a category can hold child categories; the inset grows with depth.
- Three ways to crea

te one: the Workspace actions menu for a top-level category, the category `⋯` menu for a
child, and

**Move to category** on a session row.
- The category `⋯` menu: new child / rename / delete. Renamin

g is an **inline input** (Enter commits, Escape
cancels) — no dialog.
### 2. Drag gestures
Five gestures, each with its own landing rule:
| Drag this | Onto | Result |
| A session row | Another row in the flat list or a workspace group | Reorder (persisted locally) |

| A session row | A row inside a category | Reorder **within that category** |
| A session row | A c

ategory container | **Reassign** the session to that category |
| A category row | A sibling categor

y row | Reorder **among siblings** |
| A category row | The **middle band** of another category row
| Make it a **child** of that category |
A category dropped on another row's top or bottom edge sorts; dropped on the middle band it re-paren

ropped on another row's top or bottom edge sorts; dropped on the middle band it re-parents.
[该节后续省略]
## Notes and caveats

**1. Prerelease compatibility is not promised.**
The plugin targets the current dsh prerelease plugi

n APIs. When dsh upgrades, **update the plugin too** —
moving only one side easily hits a removed pa

ckage or a renamed export, and the symptom is usually a missing
sidebar block or a window that never

r a renamed export, and the symptom is usually a missing
sidebar block or a window that never opens.

**2. "Permanently delete" really deletes.**
Delete is reversible (it goes to the bin). **Permanently

delete**, **Clean up expired** and **Empty bin** are
**not**. The bin is not a backup — export anyt
hing important separately.

**3. View state lives in your browser.**
Grouping, ordering, category expansion, the archive filter

and each account's manual order all persist under
`dsh.session-categories.view.v2` in **browser loca

lStorage**. A new machine, a cleared cache or a different
profile loses them. Sessions and categorie
s themselves do not live there and survive a cache clear.

**4. Deleting a category archives its sessions.**
Recursive delete **archives** the sessions inside

(it does not delete them). Their logs are untouched and
they can be unarchived at any time.

**5. Cross-Workspace operations are refused.**
Moving a session into another Workspace's category, m

oving a category into its own descendant, or acting on a
stale revision are all rejected with a reas
on. That is protection, not a bug.

**6. Manual order needs the Manual setting.**
Left on `Last updated`, new activity keeps pushing ses
sions back to the top and overwrites the order you set.

**7. This plugin injects no global CSS.**
All styling goes through CSS Modules (hashed class names)

scoped to the DOM it renders. It does not change the
sidebar's global width, the window background,

or write to `document.body`. It therefore neither fixes nor
breaks shell-level layout problems.

**8. Uninstall.**
`dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-session-keeper`. Categories and session data
stay in dsh storage.
## Compatibility
The plugin targets the current dsh prerelease plugin APIs and is intended to work with an **unmodifi

ed** dsh
installation. dsh does not promise prerelease compatibility across versions — update dsh an

d this plugin
together when upgrading.
